title: [BUG][DeepCompile] DeepCompile fails on Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat with `RuntimeError: 'weight' must be 2-D` (LLaMA works in the same environment)
author: zuoyanzhang

comments.author: zuoyanzhang
comments.body:
Thanks. I have one question about DeepCompile support for MoE models.

Since MoE involves dynamic routing, top-k expert selection, and sparse dispatch/gather rather than a standard dense MLP path, does DeepCompile use any MoE-specific handling under torch.compile?

For the MoE results reported in the paper (e.g. Mixtral), was there any special treatment for the router / expert path, or are MoE models expected to compile through the same flow as dense models?

comments.author: eternalNight
comments.body:
I recently met the same issue on another model (qwen3.5-vl). The root cause in my case was that `self.embed_tokens(input_ids)` was followed by a graph break in a loop body in the same method, making torch dynamo skipping the whole method. During execution that method ran in eager mode **without** parameter gathering because DeepCompile had disabled it. As a result the `weight` was always shareded with a shape of `[0]`, leading to the error.

To confirm, you can enable dynamo logs by:

```python
import logging, torch
torch._logging.set_logs(dynamo=logging.INFO, graph_breaks=True)
torch._dynamo.config.verbose = True
```

and search for the following pattern in the logs:

```
Skipping frame because there is a graph break in a for/while loop
torch.compile intentionally decided to skip the frame xxx (/path/to/source line xxx) and fall back to eager.
```

Fixing that would require modifying the model implementation. In my case I need to separate the break-causing loop into a subroutine to work it around, e.g.

```python
#####
# Before
#####

def fast_pos_embed_interpolate(...):
    # The dynamic-data-dependent loop here
    ...
    pos_embeds = self.pos_embed(...)

#####
# After
#####

def fn(...):
    # The dynamic-data-dependent loop here

def fast_pos_embed_interpolate(...):
    xxx = fn(...)
    ...
    pos_embeds = self.pos_embed(...)
```

@zuoyanzhang For your case, you may first try a more recent version of transformers which seems to have the qwen2-moe model code simplified.
